textbookText: Joseph Ritter von Fraunhofer was a German physicist and optical lens manufacturer. Fraunhofer was born in Straubling, Bavaria, on March 6, 1787, and he died in Munich on June 7, 1826. He made optical glass, an achromatic telescope, and objective lenses. He also invented the spectroscope, and developed diffraction grating for producing and analyzing light spectra. He was the first to study and classify the dark lines that appear in the spectra of the sun. During his lifetime he was known as the maker of the finest refractor telescopes in Europe.

17.1 Introduction Lens is a homogenous transparent medium enclosed by two spherical refracting surfaces. Lenses are commonly used in our daily life. For example, eyeglasses, contact lenses, cameras, smartphones, microscopes, binoculars, telescopes, projectors, reading glasses, magnifying glasses, headlights, spotlights and flashlights of vehicles, eyepieces in binoculars and

microscopes, etc. Lenses are essential optical components that enable us to see objects and images clearly, capture images, explore the world around us, and enhance our visual experiences in various ways. There are mainly two types of lenses; concave and convex.

1. Convex Lens A lens thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges as shown in figure 17.1 is called a convex lens. There are of three types convex lenses. Bi-convex lens: A lens having both surfaces convex as shown in figure 17.2 (i) is a bi-convex lens. Radii of curvatures of two surfaces may or may not be equal. Plano-convex lens: A lens having one surface plane and the other surface convex as shown in figure 17.2 (ii) a plano-convex lens.

[Fig.17.1, A convex lens] [Fig. 17.2, Types of convex lenses] Concavo - convex lens: It is a lens having one surface concave and the other convex as shown in figure 17.2(iii). For this lens radius of curvature of the convex surface is less than that of the concave surface.

2. Concave Lens A lens which is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges as shown in figure 17.3 is called a concave lens. Concave lenses are of three types.
[Fig.17.3, A concave lens][Fig.17.4, Types of concave lenses]

Bi-concave lens: A lens having both surfaces concave as shown in figure 17.4 (i) is a biconcave lens. Radii of curvatures of two surfaces may or may not be equal. Plano-concave lens: It is a lens having one surface plane and the other surface concave as shown in figure 17.4 (ii). Convexo – concave lens: It is a lens having one surface convex and the other concave as shown in figure 17.4 (iii). The radius of curvature of the concave surface is less than that of the convex surface.

Properties of Spherical Lenses The properties of lenses determine their optical behavior. Therefore, it is important to understand the properties of spherical lenses for their proper design, and for using them in various applications effectively to ensure proper focus, image clarity, and optical performance. Important properties of spherical lenses are explained below. Focal Length (f): It is the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus of a lens. The focal length determines the conversing as well as the diverging power of a lens. A lens with a shorter focal length has a stronger converging power whereas a lens with a longer focal length has a weaker converging power. Optical Power (P): The optical power is the measure of the ability of a lens to bend (converse or diverge) the rays of light. It is expressed as reciprocal to the focal length so that the focal length must be in meter. Therefore, the power of lens, P = 1 . A lens with a higher optical f power bends the light more strongly than a lens with a lower optical power. Shape of Lens: Spherical lenses have a characteristic shape. One or both the surfaces of a spherical lens are the portions of a sphere. The shape of a lens may be concave or convex. Aperture: The aperture of a lens is the effective diameter of the lens through which light passes. The amount of light that can enter the lens depends on its aperture. It also affects the brightness of the image formed.
